This term translates to 'arrows' and evokes projectiles launched with precision. In the Bible, arrows can symbolize God's judgments or the attacks of the enemy. In this verse, they represent divine actions that impact the world, emphasizing that God is in control and acts according to His will. This reminds us that God is both a protector and a judge.

This word means 'cloud' and is often associated with God's presence. Clouds in the Bible can symbolize both the mystery of God and His closeness. In this verse, the clouds pouring out water are an image of divine power manifesting in nature, highlighting that God uses even elements to accomplish His purposes. This teaches us that God is sovereign over all creation.

18.epoque: Psalm 77 is attributed to Asaph, a choir leader during the time of David, situating this writing in a period of Israel's history where worship and music were central to the spiritual life of the people.
18.passage: This psalm expresses deep distress and a cry to God in times of crisis. The chapter recalls memories of God's mighty acts in the past, contrasting with present pain, and highlights the struggle between faith and despair.
18.culture: In Hebrew culture, natural phenomena like thunder and storms were often perceived as manifestations of divine power. Songs and psalms were means to remind the community of God's interventions in history.
18.interpretation: The verse evokes a powerful image of God's presence in moments of crisis. The clouds, thunder, and arrows symbolize divine anger, but also His ability to intervene and protect His people. This reminds us that even in life's storms, God is present and active.
18.commentaire: This verse teaches us that God is sovereign over nature and that He uses even elements to manifest His power. In our own storms, we can remember that God is by our side, ready to act. In times of trouble, it is essential to turn to Him in faith, knowing that He hears our cries and has the power to transform our trials into testimonies of His greatness.

mots.sens: This term refers to a tremor or a jerky movement, often associated with manifestations of divine power. It evokes not only the shaking of the earth but also the agitation that accompanies the presence of God. In this verse, it emphasizes the reaction of creation in the face of God's majesty and power, reminding us that even nature is sensitive to His voice.

This word means lightning or sudden light, often used to describe spectacular manifestations of divine power. In the context of this verse, it symbolizes God's revelation through impressive natural phenomena, illustrating His sovereignty and ability to intervene in the world. It reminds believers that God's light can pierce the darkness and bring clarity and direction.

This term refers to a whirlwind or a storm, often associated with chaotic and powerful events. In the biblical context, it can symbolize the trials and struggles that believers go through, but also the power of God that can use them to accomplish His purposes. It reminds us that even in the midst of life's storms, God is present and active.

19.epoque: Psalm 77 is generally attributed to a period of crisis or distress, likely during the exile or a time of suffering for the people of Israel, when faith was tested.
19.passage: This passage is part of a psalm that expresses the author's pain and inner struggle in the face of desperate circumstances, while recalling God's powerful interventions in the past.
19.culture: In Hebrew culture, manifestations of nature were often seen as signs of divine action. Storms and lightning were powerful symbols of God's presence and His ability to judge and save.
19.interpretation: This verse highlights God's majesty revealed in nature, reminding believers that even in turbulent moments, God is sovereign. It invites us to recognize His power and turn to Him in our moments of despair.
19.commentaire: This passage teaches us that the trials and storms of life are not signs of God's absence, but rather opportunities to see His power at work. In times of trouble, we must remember that God is always present and active, ready to intervene in our lives. This encourages us to have faith in His sovereignty and to seek His light in our darkness.

mots.sens: This word means 'to find' or 'to discover.' It evokes the idea of revelation or unexpected appearance. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes that God has opened a way in impossible circumstances, thus demonstrating His sovereignty and power. Spiritually, it reminds us that God can bring forth solutions where we see no way out.

Meaning 'way' or 'path,' this term is often used in the Bible to denote the direction or course one takes in life. In this verse, it symbolizes divine guidance in moments of distress. Theologically, it teaches us that God charts paths for His people, even in the darkest moments.

This word refers to the sea or great waters, often symbolizing chaos or trials in the Bible. In the context of this verse, it represents the seemingly insurmountable obstacles that God overcomes. It reminds us that even in desperate situations, God is capable of creating order from chaos.

This term means 'sign' or 'mark.' It evokes the idea of something that leaves a mark or testimony. In this verse, it emphasizes that God's traces are not always visible, but this does not diminish His powerful action in our lives. Spiritually, it invites us to trust God even when we cannot see His works.

20.epoque: This psalm was written in a context of suffering and anguish, likely during the exile or a period of crisis for the people of Israel.
20.passage: Psalm 77 expresses deep distress but also reflection on God's past works, particularly the Exodus. This verse recalls how God intervened miraculously in Israel's history.
20.culture: In Hebrew culture, the sea and great waters often represent chaotic and untamed forces, symbolizing the trials and dangers faced by the people.
20.interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's ability to open paths where there are none, thus demonstrating His sovereign power. Spiritually, it reminds us that even in our moments of despair, God is at work and capable of guiding us through life's storms.
20.commentaire: This psalm encourages us to remember God's past interventions in our lives and to have faith in His ability to act today. Even when we do not see His traces, we can be assured that He is present and opening paths for us. In our moments of crisis, let us trust in His guidance and power.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to stand' or 'to be established.' In the context of the leadership of the people of Israel, it evokes the idea of firmness and stability. The root of this word implies a notion of permanence and support, highlighting God's faithfulness to His people. Spiritually, it reminds us that God is our rock, our refuge, who supports us in times of uncertainty.

This term translates to 'judgment' or 'decision.' It refers to the idea of divine justice and order established by God. In the context of the leadership of the people, it means that God guides His people according to just and equitable principles. Theologically, it reminds us that God is a just judge and directs our lives according to His perfect wisdom.

This word means 'people' or 'multitude.' It evokes the idea of a united community, under the direction of a shepherd. In the context of the verse, it emphasizes the responsibility of Moses and Aaron as leaders chosen by God to guide His people. Spiritually, it reminds us of the importance of the community of believers and unity in faith.

This verb means 'to shepherd' or 'to lead.' It is often used to describe the role of a shepherd who cares for his flock. In this verse, it emphasizes how God cares for His people through His servants. Theologically, it reminds us that God is our shepherd, who guides and protects us in our spiritual walk.

21.epoque: This psalm is generally attributed to the period of the Exodus, when the people of Israel were on their way to the Promised Land, under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
21.passage: Psalm 77 evokes Asaph's lamentations in the face of the people's trials, but he remembers God's faithfulness in the past, particularly during the liberation from Egypt.
21.culture: In Israelite culture, the role of shepherd was crucial, symbolizing protection, guidance, and care. Leaders were often seen as spiritual shepherds guiding the people toward safety and prosperity.
21.interpretation: This verse highlights how God directed His people through human leaders, affirming the importance of divine guidance in our lives. It reminds us that even in moments of doubt, God is always at work to lead His people toward His promise.
21.commentaire: This passage encourages us to recognize God's hand in our daily lives. Just as Moses and Aaron were instruments of God to guide His people, we are called to be witnesses of His faithfulness and to lead others to Him. As believers, we must remember that God is our shepherd, and we can trust Him to lead us on the right path.
